preconditions.description: Input is a non-empty string of small Latin letters with length between 1 and 10^5.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(xi) <= len(stdin) for xi, li in (line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: Each starting position xi is within the bounds of the input string length.

postconditions.expression: all(int(li) > 0 for xi, li in (line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: Each length li is positive (non-empty parts).

postconditions.expression: sum(int(li) for xi, li in (line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])) == max_possible_length
postconditions.description: The sum of all li values is maximized, where max_possible_length is the length of the longest possible password that can be reconstructed from the input string under the given rules.
The first line of the output is an integer k (number of non-empty parts), followed by exactly k lines of xi and li pairs.

postconditions.expression: all(int(xi) < int(xj) for i, j in [(i, j) for i in range(k) for j in range(i+1, k)])
postconditions.description: The starting positions xi are in strictly increasing order.

postconditions.expression: any(int(li) % 2 == 1 for xi, li in (line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: At least one part has an odd length (the middle part).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(xi) + int(li) - 1 <= len(stdin) for xi, li in (line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: Each part (xi, li) is fully contained within the input string bounds.
